items.statement: submit_put_task inserts a new key synchronously under cpu_lock, get_blocking returns a lock-protected caller reference, and batched_allocate allocates directly or enters grouped eviction when capacity is exhausted.
The tests trace put, get, and remove reference-count changes and show a full pinned group blocking allocation until unpin permits eviction and allocator recovery.
Grouped eviction skips any candidate whose layer is absent or not evictable, but can evict a different fully evictable group while retaining a pinned group.
A put increments the object's reference count, adds it to hot_cache, and updates policy; pinning keeps all layer keys resident, while unpinning allows their eviction on the next allocation.
batched_allocate first requests a complete batch, frees only a complete evictable layer group, retries allocation, and the recovery test verifies allocator accounting with memcheck.

Grouped eviction treats batch_size as the layer-group width and refuses partial eviction; a capacity-sized pinned group therefore makes a non-busy-loop allocation return None without removing its keys.

get_blocking increments the caller's reference while holding cpu_lock so eviction cannot win first, and candidate validation, hot-cache removal, and allocator free occur within the same CPU critical section.

When no complete evictable group is available, batched_allocate records an eviction failure and returns None if busy looping is disabled; after unpin, the same allocation succeeds and removes the old group.

items.description: Under the CPU lock, a new put increments the MemoryObj reference count, inserts the key into hot_cache, and updates the cache policy.
items.statement: For a previously absent key, submit_put_task increments the MemoryObj reference count, stores it in hot_cache, and records the put in the cache policy while holding cpu_lock.
